# OSS Security KB Update Review

## 1. PyPI `httpx` — CVE-2021-41945 (GHSA-h8pj-cxx2-jfg2)

### Summary of Evidence

**Vulnerability:** Improper input validation in `httpx.URL`, `httpx.Client`, and `httpx.URL.copy_with`.

**Severity:** Critical (per GHSA), CVE-2021-41945.

**Fixed version — conflicting data:**

| Source | Fixed Version |
|---|---|
| GHSA-h8pj-cxx2-jfg2 | `0.23.0` |
| CVE-2021-41945 (NVD) | `< 0.23.0` affected (i.e., fixed in `0.23.0`) |
| PYSEC-2022-183 | `0.20.0` |

The GHSA advisory and the CVE description both point to **0.23.0** as the fix (corroborated by the linked release tag `0.23.0` and the referenced PR/commits). PYSEC-2022-183 lists `0.20.0` as the fixed version, which conflicts. The GHSA/CVE/upstream evidence is stronger; `0.23.0` should be treated as the authoritative fixed version.

**Note:** The GHSA summary text says "<=1.0.0.beta0" is affected, which appears to be an artifact from the original report and is misleading — the actual affected range per advisory data is `>=0, <0.23.0`.

### Suggested KB Page Update for `httpx` (PyPI)

> **CVE-2021-41945 / GHSA-h8pj-cxx2-jfg2** — Critical
>
> **Improper Input Validation** in `httpx.URL`, `httpx.Client`, and functions using `httpx.URL.copy_with`. An attacker may be able to craft URLs that bypass validation logic.
>
> - **Affected versions:** `< 0.23.0`
> - **Fixed version:** `0.23.0`
> - **⚠ Note:** PYSEC-2022-183 lists the fixed version as `0.20.0`, conflicting with the GHSA and NVD entries which both specify `0.23.0`. Upstream references (release tag, PR #2185, commit `e9b0c85`) confirm **`0.23.0`** as the fix.
> - **References:** [GHSA-h8pj-cxx2-jfg2](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h8pj-cxx2-jfg2), [Issue #2184](https://github.com/encode/httpx/issues/2184), [Release 0.23.0](https://github.com/encode/httpx/releases/tag/0.23.0)

---

## 2. Maven `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3` — CVE-2025-48924 (GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v)

### Summary of Evidence

**Vulnerability:** Uncontrolled Recursion in `ClassUtils.getClass(...)` — very long input strings cause `StackOverflowError`, which can crash an application (DoS).

**Severity:** Moderate (per GHSA / Apache advisory).

**Fixed version — no conflicts:**

All sources (GHSA, CVE, Apache mailing list advisory) consistently state:

- `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3`: affected `3.0` to `< 3.18.0`, **fixed in `3.18.0`**
- `commons-lang:commons-lang` (legacy 2.x): affected `2.0` through `2.6` — **no fix available** (2.x is end-of-life; last affected `2.6`)

### Suggested KB Page Update for `org.apache.commons:commons-lang3` (Maven)

> **CVE-2025-48924 / GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v** — Moderate
>
> **Uncontrolled Recursion (DoS)** in `ClassUtils.getClass(...)`. Very long input strings trigger a `StackOverflowError`, which is typically unhandled and can crash the application.
>
> - **Affected versions:** `>= 3.0, < 3.18.0`
> - **Fixed version:** `3.18.0`
> - **Also affects:** Legacy `commons-lang:commons-lang` 2.0–2.6 (no fix; 2.x is end-of-life). Users on 2.x should migrate to `commons-lang3` >= 3.18.0.
> - **Fix commit:** [`b424803`](https://github.com/apache/commons-lang/commit/b424803abdb2bec818e4fb
